description: The SECOND `keyword`-carrying runtime site keeps the canonical identity too (issue #741). A `map` body is a value context, so an escape inside it raises `ol-return-in-comprehension` (`spec/execution-model.md:226-227`, `spec/error-model.md:116`) rather than `ol-return-outside-proc`, even at the top level — and the EXECUTED Heritage spelling `output` reports `params` `{ keyword: "return", form: "map" }`, byte-identical to the Core twin `tests/conformance/core-language/comprehensions/comprehension-return-in-comprehension` (`:out = map n in [1] [ return :n ]`, same `params`, same `stage: "runtime"`). This site is fixtured separately from the outside-proc one because the runtime carries a SEPARATE copy of the rule for it — the defect was present at both copies, and a fixture for only one would leave the other unpinned. `params` is canonical; the `message` still names what the learner typed. The `source_span` is the whole `output :n` escape statement — the runtime's own span for this rule, which is why identity is asserted on `code` + `params` and not on the span (`spec/error-model.md:254-259`).

diagnostics.message: output doesn't belong in a map — a map reports its last expression instead.
